title: A lifted syzygy yields a degree-two class with prescribed curvature image
statement: Let $q:R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a surjection of commutative rings with kernel $(f)$ and $f^2=0$, and put $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(f)$ using the $R$-action on $(f)$ by lifts. Let $n,m\geq0$ be integers and put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with $q_P:P'\to P$ the coefficientwise map, and let $h_1,\ldots,h_m,r_1,\ldots,r_m\in P$ satisfy $\sum_jr_jh_j=0$. Assume every coefficient of every $r_j$ lies in $I$. Set $S=P/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$. Suppose $h'_j,r'_j,g'\in P'$ satisfy $q_P(h'_j)=h_j$, $q_P(r'_j)=r_j$, and $\sum_jr'_jh'_j=g'f$. Let $(A,d,\gamma)$ be a divided-power differential graded $R$-algebra [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], polynomial as a graded divided-power algebra with finitely many variables in each degree, equipped with an augmentation $A\to S$ inducing $H_0(A)\cong S$, and assume $H_1(A)=0$. Choose any graded divided-power polynomial lift $\rho:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ with the same generators and any $R'$-linear degree $-1$ signed derivation $D$ reducing to $d$ and compatible with divided powers. On $B=A/IA$ let $\theta$ be the map characterized by $D^2(a')=\iota(\theta(\overline{\rho(a')}))$, where $\iota:B\xrightarrow{\sim}fA'$ sends $\overline{\rho(a')}$ to $fa'$ [lem-sfb-square-zero-dga-curvature]. Then there is $z\in B_2$ with $dz=0$ and $[\theta(z)]=\bar g$ under $H_0(B)\cong S/IS$, where $\bar g$ is the image of $q_P(g')$.

source.place: Tag 09PT (lemma-compute-theta), statement and proof, stated for the cycle representative and the curvature construction of Tag 09PS

proof.text: Write $\epsilon:A_0\to S$ for the augmentation. Since negative degrees vanish, $H_0(A)=A_0/d(A_1)$; thus $\epsilon$ is surjective with kernel $d(A_1)$. Choose $a_i\in A_0$ mapping to the image of $x_i$ in $S$, and define $\varphi:P\to A_0$ by polynomial evaluation at the $a_i$. Then $\varphi(h_j)\in\ker\epsilon$, so choose $u_j\in A_1$ with $du_j=\varphi(h_j)$. By the homology and differential definitions in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], $v=\sum_j\varphi(r_j)u_j$ has $dv=\varphi(\sum_jr_jh_j)=0$, because $d(A_0)=0$. The hypothesis $H_1(A)=0$ gives $\xi\in A_2$ with $d\xi=v$.

source.place: Tag 09PT (lemma-compute-theta), proof, first paragraph: lift the presentation and use H_1(A)=0

proof.text: Every $\varphi(r_j)$ belongs to $IA_0$: express $r_j$ as a finite sum of monomials with coefficients in $I$ and evaluate. Hence $d\xi\in IA_1$, and the image $z$ of $\xi$ in $B_2$ is a cycle. The induced differential on $B$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-square-zero-dga-curvature]. Moreover, directly from the homology definition in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], $H_0(B)=A_0/(IA_0+d(A_1))=S/IS$, with the identification induced by $\epsilon$. Indeed $d(B_1)$ is the image of $d(A_1)$, and surjectivity of $\epsilon$ identifies the image of $IA_0$ with $IS$.

source.place: Tag 09PT (lemma-compute-theta), proof, first paragraph: reduction modulo I; Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), quotient DGA

proof.text: Use the fixed lift $A'$ and operator $D$ from the statement. Lift $a_i,u_j,\xi$ to $a'_i\in A'_0,u'_j\in A'_1,\xi'\in A'_2$, and evaluate at the $a'_i$ to define $\varphi':P'\to A'_0$ with $\rho\varphi'=\varphi q_P$. The polynomial description in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] is now explicitly by successive adjunctions. The free-module descriptions in [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] give a monomial basis: start with ordinary polynomial monomials in degree zero; at each odd adjunction multiply the old basis by $1,T$, and at each even adjunction by $T^{[a]}$ for $a\geq0$. At a union stage take all finite monomials, whose independence is checked in a stage containing them. Thus in each degree reduction applies $q$ coefficientwise in the same monomial bases, and its kernel is exactly $fA'_i$. Reducing $Du'_j-\varphi'(h'_j)$ and $D\xi'-\sum_j\varphi'(r'_j)u'_j$ gives zero by Step 1. Hence there are $b_j\in A'_0,c\in A'_1$ with $Du'_j=\varphi'(h'_j)+fb_j$ and $D\xi'=\sum_j\varphi'(r'_j)u'_j+fc$.

source.place: Tag 09PT (lemma-compute-theta), proof, second paragraph: lifts and the differential error terms

proof.text:
If $b'\in R'$ has $q(b')\in I$, then $b'f=0$, by the definition of the $R$-action on $(f)$ and of $I$. Thus every coefficient of $r'_j$ is killed by $f$, and $f\varphi'(r'_j)=0$. Since $D$ vanishes on $A'_0$ and is $R'$-linear, its signed Leibniz rule applied to Step 3 gives
$$D^2\xi'=\sum_j\varphi'(r'_jh'_j)+\sum_j f\varphi'(r'_j)b_j+fDc=f\varphi'(g')+fDc.$$
By the injective identification $\iota$ and the curvature formula in [lem-sfb-square-zero-dga-curvature], this equality says $\theta(z)=\overline{\varphi(q_P(g'))}+d\overline{\rho(c)}$ in $B_0$. Passing to the quotient defining $H_0$ [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] kills the boundary term. Under Step 2's identification with $S/IS$, the first term is $\bar g$, since $\epsilon\varphi$ is the original quotient map $P\to S$. This proves the required equality for the cycle $z$.
